vedic_reference.note: The name Nischal is derived from the Sanskrit root 'sthala' (स्थल), which has a rich history in Vedic mythology. The term 'sthala' refers to a physical or metaphysical place of stability, such as a temple or a spiritual center. In the Bhagavad Gita (2.47), Lord Krishna says, 'Among all places, I am the immovable one in the heart of all beings'. Thus, the name Nischal can be seen as a reminder of the inner stability and peace that comes from connecting with one's true self and the divine.
